sitsen-rok: A wide skirt of flowered Indian chintz. Fabrics like this came in with the Dutch East India Company and were hugely popular in the 18th-century Zaan region, where the overskirt was called a wagd.
nieuw-fries-kostuum-van-afke-wiersma: New Frisian Costume by Afke Wiersma
Launched in 1950 as a new regional dress for Friesland, mixing old Frisian dress with Dior's New Look. This version has an embroidered linen cap and a jacket and skirt of purple wool.
jongensjurkje: A woollen winter dress with pink bows, worn by a small boy. Until the late 19th century, young boys wore dresses just like girls.
kotomisi-ensemble: The koto is the dress of Creole women in Suriname, everyday wear from about 1870 and a way to send hidden messages. This is its most common form, the bigi koto.
borststuk: Part of a ten-piece parade armour that Amsterdam's civic guard ordered from northern Italy in the 1570s. It was probably made in Brescia.
mitaines-met-jak: Fingerless mitts that 19th-century Zaan women wore over their forearms, in silk, wool or cotton, often edged with bobbin lace.
keurslijf: Stiff underwear that pressed the torso into a flat cone. The shape barely changed from the late 16th century to about 1790, and lacing it tight needed a helper.
springpak-striptease-suit: A windproof suit of the British Special Operations Executive, worn over normal clothes for a parachute jump. The camouflage was painted on by hand.
driedelige-wandeljapon: Jacket, skirt and drapery in thin beige wool with blue trim. Ties in the waistband lift the overskirt, and a crinoline gave the 1860s width.
duitse-kap: Worn by married women in the Harmersbach and Kinzig valleys of the Black Forest. Unmarried women wore a cap with a wreath of glass beads instead.
ensemble-van-dior: Galliano's spring/summer 2009 look for Dior, inspired by Flemish painting and by the 1947 Bar suit of the New Look.
halskraag-van-gijs-bakker: Shown in 1967 by Gijs Bakker and Emmy van Leersum, whose large, light designs blurred jewellery, clothing and art.
draagbaar-object-van-lam-de-wolf: To wear around the neck or over the shoulder, or to hang on a wall. Its long lines refer to thread, the basis of all textile.
rokkendracht-voor-jongen: Regional dress for a boy of about two from Rouveen near Staphorst, around 1950. Small boys wore skirts too; a silver collar button set them apart from girls.
swimming-lesson-van-joyce-scott: The Swimming Lesson by Joyce Scott
Beadwork in peyote stitch from 1989. Scott uses jewellery to confront racism, sexism and violence.
growth-van-wiebke-pandikow: Plants 'grown' leaf by leaf from plastic bags: a comment on pollution and fast consumption.
kostuum-van-bas-kosters: Trousers and jacket after Zuiderzee fishermen's dress, from 'My Paper Crown', shown at Amsterdam Fashion Week in 2017. The fabric was block-printed in India.
luipaardmantel-van-fong-leng-0: Gold leather with leather leopards and rosettes, one of Fong Leng's best-known 1970s pieces. Mathilde Willink wore it.
pliseerockchen-van-vera-siemund: A bridal necklace inspired by pleated Biedermeier skirts, with little bells on a gold chain.
intifada-jurk: An embroidered Palestinian 'flag dress' in the colours of the Palestinian flag, made in Syria in the 1990s by Palestinian refugees as a form of protest.
ruitermantel-van-ernst-casimir: A wide grey wool coat with shoulder flaps, probably worn by Ernst Casimir of Nassau-Dietz at the siege of Roermond in 1632.
kledingset-norine: A 1930s blouse and skirt from the Brussels couture house Norine, known for its avant-garde touch.
jurk-van-iris-van-herpen: Look 9 from Escapism (2011). Metal thread woven into silk lets the fabric be shaped like sculpture.
matrozenpak: A boy's sailor suit sewn in secret from orange and white cloth during the German occupation: a sign of scarce textile and of quiet defiance.
bruidsjapon: Wedding dress of Henriëtte van Cleeff
White satin with a train and beading, made for an Amsterdam wedding in 1882 by the dressmaker Lina de Goede.
tuniek-van-paco-rabanne: Small metal plates linked by rings, typical of Rabanne's futuristic 1960s 'chainmail' dresses.
halve-rouw-jurkje-van-prinses-wilhelmina: After her father died in 1890, the ten-year-old queen moved from full black to 'half mourning': white cotton with black motifs and edges.
jurk-marinero-33-van-jef-montes: Jacquard-woven from experimental yarns that change shape for good when exposed to the weather.
silhouet-van-walter-van-beirendonck: By one of the Antwerp designers who put Belgian avant-garde fashion on the world map from the mid-1980s.
oorijzer-uit-west-friesland: An early, rare ear iron that held a lace cap in place. Most were melted down when fashions changed.
hoofdsieraad-van-nicolaas-van-beek: Head ornament by Nicolaas van Beek
Sawn and bent sheet metal, a wearable object from the Space Age 1960s.
kostuum-van-een-zoeaaf: Worn by Catholic volunteers who defended the Papal States for Pope Pius IX in the 1860s.
zijden-japon: A high waist and short puffed sleeves: the Empire style that came from France in the early 19th century.
kachelpijp-collier-van-gijs-bakker: Two pieces of anodised stovepipe: a 'ready-made' and a classic of Dutch jewellery design.
korte-schoudermantel-van-koningin-wilhel: Short evening cape of Queen Wilhelmina
A short cape (sortie) worn over gala evening dress, together with long white gloves.
filigrein-armband-uit-indonesie: Gold filigree and granulation of great precision, probably by a goldsmith in Kendari.
bootjesketting: A gold necklace set with garnets, worn by Zaan women over the neckerchief with their regional dress.
rococo-collier-van-evert-nijland: Nijland combines materials like silver, silk, glass and porcelain, often referring to rococo and baroque art.
akhnif-amazigh-mantel: A warm wool cloak for the Atlas Mountains, worn by Muslim and Jewish men in Morocco until the 1950s. Also called a burnous.
avondjapon-met-pailletten-van-mme-wiegan: Sequinned evening dress by Mme Wiegandt-Riccard
Black tulle covered in celluloid sequins, glass beads and jet, with a train.
volendamse-hul: The icon of Volendam's Sunday dress. Its pointed shape only took form between 1905 and 1910.
jeanne-lanvin: Robe de style ‘Le souffle’ by Jeanne Lanvin
A low 1920s waist with a full skirt that recalls French court dress: Lanvin's trademark.
ottomaanse-bruidsjurk: Velvet with gold couching. The gold and the skill in a bindalli showed the wearer's status.
mourning-piece-van-lucy-sarneel: Inspired by the square chest cloth of Marken dress, which turned black and white in mourning.
hindelooper-bruid: A bridal coat (wentke) of chintz painted with red flowers on white, with accessories in Indian checked cotton.
ceintuur-van-meret-oppenheim: Designed by the surrealist in the 1930s and only made in 2003, from her sketches.
rokkostuum-van-j-campbell-latham-co: Tailcoat by J. Campbell, Latham & Co
outfit-punker: Torn clothes and safety pins from Rotterdam's early-1980s punk scene, a youth revolt against the establishment.
ensemble-van-rich-mnisi: From 'Hiya Kaya', spring/summer 2021, by a South African label that retells African heritage for today.
galafhofkostuum-van-de-opperjagermeester: Court gala uniform of the Master of the Hunt
Dark green, not the usual court blue. Nine embroidered branches on the chest mark his rank.
volendams-jak-van-neeltje-schilder: Printed black cotton for housework, shaped by gathering the fabric around the bust.
korte-galajapon-van-prinses-juliana: Short gala dress of Princess Juliana
Ordered from the Paris house Premet when Juliana came of age and took on official duties.
pashtun-bruidsensemble: Shiny fabric, mirrors and metal thread from Afghanistan, made to catch the light and every eye.
ensemble-brabantse-streekdracht: Plain black dress of around 1900 that served for church, mourning and parties alike.
habit-la-francaise: An 18th-century man's suit of coat, waistcoat and breeches, embroidered with wild flowers.
oranje-boven-van-marion-herbst: By a co-founder of the 'rebellious goldsmiths', who worked early with perspex, aluminium and acrylic.
staatsiejas-van-de-sultans-van-yogyakart: State coat of the sultans of Yogyakarta
A patchwork coat, sacred in Central Java, worn by two 19th-century sultans at court processions.
silhouet-van-jan-jan-van-essche: Look AW23/P#11, in hand-woven checked wool by the Senegalese artist Lamine Diouf.
japon-met-strompelrok-van-loelgen-kriege: Pink satin, silk gauze and embroidered tulle, cut narrow at the ankles.
wambuis-van-hugo-de-groot: Leather, long-sleeved. Tradition says the scholar wore it when he escaped Loevestein Castle in a book chest.
jas-van-yamuna-forzani: Psychedelic colour and camp from spring/summer 2018, challenging the line between menswear and womenswear.
amazone-kostuum: A dark blue riding habit, with elastic bands inside the skirt to hold the leg while riding.
zeventiende-eeuwse-herenhoed: A yellow felt hat, found inside an old wall of Utrecht's orphanage during demolition.
babyjasje-met-zaans-stikwerk: Thick quilted cotton with stitched patterns, warm and costly to make.
bruidskimono: White damask with phoenixes and a tortoiseshell pattern, all symbols of long life.
beatles-dress: A 1964 print with portraits and signatures of the four Beatles, from a weaving mill in Enschede.
trui-van-loes-veenstra: One of 550 hand-knitted sweaters by a Rotterdam woman who knitted for decades and never wore them.
zwangerschaps-ensemble: Home-made maternity wear from the 1960s, with an adjustable skirt.
ghanese-ensemble-voor-i-care: Made in green and white, the colours of the I Care foundation, which together mean 'Go Ahead'.
trouw-en-rouwensemble: Black, because the bride's father had just died. Worn at a wedding in Utrecht in 1879.
kamerjas-van-sits: A flowered dressing gown imported from India, a fashion of the 17th and 18th centuries.
roze-sitsen-jak: An 18th-century jacket remade for a girl's Zaan regional dress in the 19th century.
trouwkostuum-isabella-stinstra: Striped shot silk from a Harlingen wedding in 1782, with French and English influences.
vilten-bruidsjurk-van-claudy-jongstra: Felt wedding dress by Claudy Jongstra
Felt of Dutch wool and Japanese silk, with a waistband that recalls an obi. Designed by Arlette Muschter.
goudgeborduurde-schoenen: Red velvet with gilt silver thread from about 1620, owned by a rich Frisian family.
zwarte-avondjurk: Beaded silk crêpe with a low waist and a short, pointed hem, made for dancing in the 1920s.
innu-jagersjas: Caribou leather, cut like an 18th-century French officer's coat, by the Innu of Quebec and Labrador.
muts-voor-opknapdracht: Machine lace and folded ribbon, from the regional dress of Oldebroek.
water-gold-sari-van-rahul-mishra: Water Gold sari by Rahul Mishra
Hand-embroidered in gold with 3D details, from a collection about the cosmos.
rijglijf: Green silk taffeta with pink shoulder ribbons.
theater-jurk-gedragen-door-louisette-0: Black stage dress worn by Louisette
Black satin with sequinned flowers, for the singer known as the Dutch Mistinguett.
theater-jurk-gedragen-door-louisette: Cream stage dress worn by Louisette
Satin with gold sequins and cherries, lined in bright pink that flashed as she danced.
kostuum-gedragen-door-louisette: A 1920s satin stage costume with sequins, drapery and a shawl.
nationale-feestrok: The Liberation Skirt, an icon of Dutch liberation, worn at national celebrations from 1945.
parels-van-makkum-van-alexander-van-slob: Pearls of Makkum by Alexander van Slobbe
Earthenware 'pearls' made by Royal Tichelaar Makkum, in an edition of 100.
maskeradekostuum-van-simon-van-gijn: Masquerade costume of Simon van Gijn
Designed by himself for the Leiden student masquerade of 1860.
rajput-bruidegom: Red silk embroidered in gold thread (zari), worn by a groom in India.
ensemble-brabantse-werkdracht: Dark, practical clothes for farm work in early 20th-century Brabant.
jurk-8-pieces-van-claes-iversen: A strapless dress from 2014, embroidered all over, partly with parts of tools.
peranakan-bruid: Yellow with dragons and phoenixes, mixing a Chinese bridal costume with Indonesian design.
adams-apple-van-sari-rathel: From 'Gender Blender', which enlarges male and female features to question gender roles.
rood-zwempak: A one-piece cotton swimsuit from the early 1900s, made for more freedom to move.
trui-van-issey-miyake: The sculptural '3D Spike' of autumn/winter 1988/89, from Miyake's first pleating experiments.
theaterkostuum-gentleman-dark-lady-van-r: Gentleman's costume for ‘Dark Lady’ by Rien Bekkers
From the 1999 production Dark Lady, by one of the best-known Dutch costume designers.
tutu-uit-doornroosje: A classical tutu of short, stiff tulle layers, for a 1968 Dutch production.
bruidsrijglijf-uit-marken: An embroidered bodice kept for Whitsun and weddings.
theaterkostuum-dark-lady-van-rien-bekker: Stage costume ‘Dark Lady’ by Rien Bekkers
Another of Bekkers' costumes for the 1999 production Dark Lady.
hoed-van-koningin-wilhelmina: Worn in 1897 when the young queen acted in plays at Het Loo Palace for her mother's birthday.
doopjurk-van-parachute: Christening gown made from a parachute
Post-war fabric was scarce, so parachute silk became wedding and christening dresses.
halssieraad-van-iradj-moini: Costume jewellery by an Iranian-born designer who made his name in New York.
trouwjapon-cornelia-agatha-vriesendorp: Wedding dress of Cornelia Agatha Vriesendorp
Moiré silk from 1864, when the white wedding dress caught on in upper-class circles.
daagse-zomerdracht-uit-marken: A Marken man's everyday summer clothes around 1950, from shirt to clogs and cap.
jurk-cirkels-van-stina-randestad: A circular design, machine-knitted from recycled textile.
mantelpak-met-hoed: A women's suit of the 1910s, modern because it let women walk and move freely.
matrozenpakje: A children's classic made popular by Queen Victoria and affordable through ready-to-wear, here from Gerzon.
herenkraammuts: New 18th-century fathers wore a quilted cap like this to receive visitors after a birth.
charm-chain-van-studio-job: A modern take on the charm bracelet, which carries memories of people.
dubbele-muts-met-kroon-uit-west-brabant: Double cap with crown from West Brabant
Pleated lace over a black undercap, for weddings and Sundays around 1900.
middeleeuwse-trip: A wooden overshoe that kept shoes out of the mud, found in an excavation in Dordrecht.
theaterschoenen-hamlet-van-rien-bekkers: Stage shoes for ‘Hamlet’ by Rien Bekkers
From Bekkers' costumes for a 1986 Hamlet.
molensteenkraag-der-fliegende-hollander-: Ruff for ‘Der Fliegende Holländer’ by Lioba Winterhalder
A 17th-century-style ruff with pearls, worn in a 1983 production of Wagner's opera.
sami-bruidsjurk-van-berit-oskal-eira: Sámi wedding clothes by Berit Oskal Eira
Made by the bride for herself and her husband, and worn on special days after the wedding too.
trouwjurk-van-hirsch-cie: Made to measure in 1915 by Amsterdam's grand fashion house for the elite.
cocon-van-chequita-nahar: Inspired by the traditional jewellery of Suriname and what it means to its wearers.
japon-met-schapenboutmouwen: Brown silk with huge sleeves, let out for a pregnancy and taken in again.
galajapon-van-koningin-wilhelmina: A Premet dress from Paris, altered for her 25th wedding anniversary in 1926.
koreaanse-bruidegom: A round-collared robe with a winged black hat, after court dress of the Joseon dynasty.
werkpak-urker-visser: Sturdy cotton that started black and faded with washing until it was only fit for work.
japanse-kimono: Affordable, shiny silk with a blurred ikat-like pattern, the fashion for daily wear in 1920s–30s Japan.
streepjes-beest-van-felieke-van-der-lees: Striped Beast by Felieke van der Leest
Crochet and textile in a wearable animal sculpture.
patchwork-ensemble-van-tess-van-zalinge: Patchwork ensemble by Tess van Zalinge
halssieraad-van-nel-linssen: Folded paper in two colours, turned into a firm structure.
jumlo-jurk-uit-pakistan: Black cotton with rich geometric embroidery, from the mountains of Kohistan.
kinderpak-van-marga-groen: Corduroy trousers, a sweater of leftover wool and a hand-made jacket from 1970s Amsterdam.
verkleedjapon-robe-langlaise: An 18th-century silk damask wedding dress, remade around 1890 for dressing-up parties.
gujarati-kap: A child's sun cap from Kutch, embroidered with flowers and small mirrors (shisha).
wapenrok-van-alet-pilon-0: A breastplate of folded canvas that hides and reshapes the body instead of showing it.
